headline: SILVER EXPLODES TO $76 AS US-IRAN CEASEFIRE EXTENDED 60 DAYS: HORMUZ REOPEN HOPES SURGE
snippet: Silver futures surged to $76.02/oz at Friday's open — a 4.6% overnight jump — after the U.S. and Iran agreed to a 60-day ceasefire extension that markets hope will reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease the inflation pressure that has weighed on precious metals positioning all month.

headline: PANAMA DROPS COBRE AUDIT ON FIRST QUANTUM AS ANTI-MINING PROTESTS REIGNITE IN STREETS
snippet: Panama released the SGS environmental audit of First Quantum's shuttered Cobre Panama copper mine on May 29 as fresh street protests flare against a possible restart. President Mulino will decide the fate of the operation — 350,000t/yr copper before its 2023 shutdown, contributing 5% of Panama's GDP — after reviewing the findings.

headline: BASE METALS HIT MONTHLY PEAK: COPPER ON PACE FOR BEST MONTH SINCE JANUARY ON IRAN DEAL
snippet: Copper and industrial metals are tracking their strongest monthly gain since January as easing Middle East tensions reduce inflation risk and lift risk appetite. Traders are now pricing in the possibility that a full ceasefire could permanently reopen Hormuz shipping lanes, removing a key commodity supply premium.

headline: GOLD'S 'HIGHER FOR LONGER' STORY IS MISSING THE STRUCTURAL BULL CASE, ANALYST ARGUES
snippet: A GoldSeek analyst argues that markets focused on prolonged rate pressure are ignoring the more powerful structural driver: sustained central bank diversification away from the dollar that makes gold's bull case much larger than traditional rate correlations would suggest.

headline: MARYLAND RESTORES GOLD AND SILVER SALES TAX EXEMPTION AFTER DEALER REVOLT CUT TRAFFIC 72%
snippet: Maryland Governor Wes Moore signed legislation restoring the state's precious metals sales tax exemption, effective July 1, after a 2025 policy change — which put Maryland at odds with 44 other U.S. states — triggered a 72% drop in showroom traffic at one major coin and bullion dealer.

headline: WHITE GOLD CORP STARTS ITS BIGGEST-EVER YUKON DRILL CAMPAIGN AHEAD OF MAIDEN PEA
snippet: White Gold Corp. kicked off its largest-ever diamond drilling program on May 28, targeting four near-surface gold deposits across the White Gold District in Yukon. A maiden preliminary economic assessment is expected in the near term, with the campaign also spinning out several critical mineral properties into W2 Critical Minerals Corp.

headline: NOVA MINERALS LAUNCHES $60M ALASKA DUAL-TRACK: 10,000m GOLD DRILL PLUS DOD-BACKED ANTIMONY
snippet: Nova Minerals commenced its fully funded 2026 program at Alaska's Estelle Gold and Critical Minerals Project on May 28, deploying three diamond rigs for 10,000m of gold drilling at RPM (recent results include 43m @ 4.4 g/t Au) while advancing DoD-funded pilot-scale domestic antimony production toward a late-2026 launch.

headline: BAYHORSE SILVER COMPLETES UNDERGROUND DRILL PREP; 2,000m PHASE 1 STARTS JUNE 1
snippet: Bayhorse Silver Inc. announced that underground drilling preparations at the Bayhorse Silver Mine are complete and Phase 1 diamond drilling — 2,000 metres — will start June 1, 2026, marking the return to systematic underground definition drilling.

headline: MINRES REBOOTS BALD HILL LITHIUM AFTER 18-MONTH PAUSE AS PRICES RECOVER SHARPLY
snippet: Mineral Resources has restarted Western Australia's Bald Hill lithium mine — shut down in November 2024 — targeting 165,000t/yr of spodumene concentrate as prices recover on China's VAT rebate changes and surging battery storage demand. The restart puts MinRes in a structurally unique position operating three independent hard-rock lithium mines.

headline: NEWMONT VS SSR MINING: WHICH GOLD STOCK CAPTURES MORE UPSIDE AT $4,500/oz GOLD?
snippet: Motley Fool analysts pit Newmont — the world's largest gold miner — against a recovering SSR Mining, dissecting AISC trajectories, production pipelines, and balance sheet health to determine which offers better leverage to $4,500/oz gold and which stock has more room to close the persistent gap with the metal itself.
